description: The plot illustrates the relationship between an unlabeled variable on the x-axis and three different accuracy metrics, represented by lines with error bars. The x-axis is unlabeled, featuring a linear scale that ranges from 0.91 to 0.99 with tick marks at intervals of 0.01, and the tick labels are rotated diagonally. The y-axis is labeled "Accuracy" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The "Final Accuracy" is represented by a solid blue line with circular markers; it begins at an x-value of approximately 0.912 with a y-value of 0.91, rises to a peak of 1.0 at x=0.932, experiences a slight decline to 0.95 at x=0.942, drops to a low of 0.86 at x=0.962, and then fluctuates before ending at x=0.992 with a y-value of 0.92. The "$\Delta$ Accuracy" is shown as a dashed orange line with diamond markers; it starts at x=0.912 with a y-value of 0.55, peaks at x=0.922 with a y-value of 0.67, generally declines with some fluctuation to reach its lowest point of 0.1 at x=0.982, and ends at x=0.992 with a y-value of 0.16. The "Initial Accuracy" is depicted by a dash-dot green line with square markers; it begins at x=0.912 with a y-value of 0.36, dips to 0.27 at x=0.922, rises to 0.59 at x=0.962, drops to 0.42 at x=0.972, sharply increases to a peak of 0.88 at x=0.982, and concludes at x=0.992 with a y-value of 0.77.
